w: In the evening assembly, on behalf of the Mayor and citizens of Atlanta, Mr. Greg Pridgeon - Deputy Chief of Staff, honored Swamishri with the 'Dream Realized Award'. The award is presented to unique personalities in memory of Dr. Martin Luther King.

As part of the Karyakar Din program, a drama presentation showed that an ideal karyakar (volunteer) should have an organized and spotless life; and should sacrifice his mind, body and wealth in the service of Satsang. In his blessings Swamishri emphasized the importance of God's infinite strength: "One who sets out to serve faces obstacles and difficulties. But if one is grounded in Dharma (morality) and God's strength then one will achieve success. The Pandavas had nothing, whereas the Kauravas had a massive army of mighty warriors. But the Pandavas had the strength of Bhagwan Krishna and that is why they won. Similarly, if we rely on God's strength then we will attain success in our works."

During the special Kishore Day assembly in the evening, the Kishores performed a folk dance and a drama reflecting the challenges that satsangi Kishores face in society. Swamishri's blessings infused moral strength in the Kishores. 550 Kishores and Kishories were present during the Kishore Day program. Thereafter Swamishri attended the Shikshapatri discourse (parayan) by Viveksagar Swami.
Pramukh Swami Maharaj Arrives in Chicago Sadhus and devotees enthusiastically received Swamishri as his car entered the Mandir and Haveli complex.

In the evening welcome assembly, BAPS trustees and directors welcomed Swamishri by offering garlands and flowers to him. The Consul General of India, Arunkumar, was present in the assembly and praised the beauty of the Chicago Mandir and Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi, India. Finally, blessing the assembly, Swamishri stated the importance of keeping faith and explained how to maintain peace of mind. In the end, he conveyed that the ultimate goal of life is to become aksharrup and worship Purushottam.

The day was celebrated as ‘Prapti Day’. Sadhus and youths sang bhajans related to prapti – the divine joy of having attained God and his God-realized Sadhu.In the evening Sunday satsang assembly Viveksagar Swami delivered a discourse. Then children and youths performed a welcome dance before Swamishri. Thereafter, Swamishri was honoured with garlands by senior sadhus. A drama on prapti, written by Yogendra Swami, was enacted by youths. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly, “If one has attained God and realized his divine happiness then one finds material happiness to be fleeting. Real happiness lies in God, in doing his bhajan. Happiness lies in spiritual association with the God-realized Sadhu. Mira found happiness in God’s bhajan but not in the pleasures of her palace and opulence. The same happened to Narsinh Mehta. Parvatbhai and Govardhanbhai were also such devotees in the time of Shriji Maharaj. They were joyous because of their association with God. God has given us intelligence therefore we should contemplate on this subject, but not remain immersed in worldly happiness.”

Dineshbhai, the sarpanch (village head) of Mendarda village in the Junagadh region, came for darshan. Before coming into satsang he had been a hardened drinker and a liquor trader. He had sold liquor by the truckload, but drawn by Pramukh Swami Maharaj's personality, he had come all the way to Bochasan with the resolve to give up this business and his addiction.

When this was told to Swamishri, Swamishri too became enthusiastic and, patting him twice, said, "It is a very good resolve. God will make you very happy. Understand that God has saved you. Now you are not to fall into this sin again or make anyone else fall into it. So once you have given it up, it is given up. Now keep to it even at the cost of your life."
Having said this, Swamishri gave him the vartman (initiation vows) and made him a follower of Shriji Maharaj, and at the same time lovingly placed a blockade on an evil prevalent in society.

A group of 52 kishore and kishori karyakars from various North American centers participated in the 2011 India Trip from June 26 to August 2, 2011. The trip helped strengthen the participants' personal satsang and provided them the opportunity to explore India's culture and sacred landscapes. Highlights of the trip included time spent in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj and a satsang shibir in Gandhinagar titled, "Brahmvidya ni College".

In the first week of their 38-day trip, the delegates traveled in the Rajasthan region, visiting Jaipur, Jodhpur, Ranakpur, Udaipur, Pindwara, Mount Abu etc. Thereafter, the kishores and kishoris went to Bharuch to receive blessings from Swamishri before going to Gandhinagar for a seven-day shibir.

The revered swamis from Amdavad, Sarangpur, and Gandhinagar led the delegates through a series of lectures and workshops on the fundamentals of Akshar Purushottam philosophy in theory and practice. As part of the shibir, the attendees also engaged in a variety of daily service activities. By participating in the shibir, the delegates strengthened their spiritual foundation and their relationship with God and Guru. The delegates then continued their pilgrimage in Gujarat, visiting various sacred places of the Swaminarayan Sampraday, including Bochasan, Chansad, Gadhada, Junagadh, Mehlav, etc. Furthermore, in the tribal areas of Tithal, they also visited the homes of local karyakars and satsangis and got a first-hand look at Swamishri's selfless efforts.

The attendees then concluded their trip with Swamishri's darshan in Mumbai. The kishores and kishoris returned home spiritually reinvigorated, taking with them messages of the shibir as well as friends and memories to last a lifetime.

Today, when Mahant Swami Maharaj sat on his bed, he began meeting the sadhus sitting in front of him for the bedtime darshan through his glance, bowing to them with folded hands. When he had finished folding his hands to everyone, he said, "Thirty nine." That is, there were 39 sadhus in front of him. Everyone was amazed; Swamishri had even counted how many sadhus there were!
